core_obligations: Choose the local presentation: apply the localisation lemma for differentials to get a diagram with a and b surjective and U, V schemes over S, so that the sheaf of differentials can be compared on the presented piece (proof lines 1023-1025).

Compute on the presentation: use the compatibility of the sheaf of differentials with the diagram to identify Omega_{X/Y}|_U with Omega_{U/V}, which is quasi-coherent because it is the sheaf of differentials of a morphism of schemes (proof lines 1026-1028).

Conclude quasi-coherence on X: the characterisation of quasi-coherent modules on an algebraic space by their restrictions to the members of a presentation applies and gives that Omega_{X/Y} is quasi-coherent (proof lines 1029-1031).
proof_roadmap: Take a presentation diagram with surjective a, b and U, V schemes (proof lines 1023-1025).
Identify the restriction of Omega_{X/Y} to U with Omega_{U/V} and note the latter is quasi-coherent (proof lines 1026-1028).
Apply the quasi-coherence criterion for algebraic spaces to finish (proof lines 1029-1031).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for a morphism of algebraic spaces f : X -> Y over a scheme S the sheaf of differentials Omega_{X/Y} is a quasi-coherent O_X-module (statement lines 1018-1019). The proof is a reduction to the scheme case along a presentation: the localisation lemma supplies a diagram with surjective maps from schemes U and V, the restriction of Omega_{X/Y} to U is identified with Omega_{U/V}, which is quasi-coherent by the scheme-theoretic statement, and quasi-coherence on X follows from the criterion phrased in terms of a presentation (proof lines 1023-1031). The two steps that carry the content are the identification on the presented piece and the appeal to the presentation criterion. The claim is H2: no construction beyond the diagram, three cited inputs.
